claim: The survey explicitly states that existing offline-MBO benchmarks fail to distinguish whether performance gains come from surrogate modeling, optimization strategy, or chance, and calls this an open future-work need rather than a solved problem.

claim: The survey identifies benchmark reliability problems in offline MBO, including that some benchmarks (TFB8, TFB10) have search spaces so constrained that simple gradient ascent already performs well, making it hard to distinguish sophisticated algorithms.
stance_target: N8: platform/library-version dependence and benchmark-sensitivity discussion in offline MBO
quoted_support: Current scientific design benchmarks in offline MBO face two major challenges. First, due to the difficulty of collecting labeled data, some benchmarks—such as TFB8 and TFB10 (Barrera et al., 2016)—offer overly constrained search spaces where even simple gradient ascent methods can achieve impressive results, making it difficult to distinguish the performance of more sophisticated algorithms.
